mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about equal sets reflects a common misconception?

options.A: Two sets are equal if they contain exactly the same elements.
options.B: Two sets are equal if they have the same number of elements, regardless of what the elements are.
options.C: The empty set is equal only to itself.
options.D: If A = {1,2,3} then B = {3,2,1} is equal to A.

mcqs.answer: Two sets are equal if they have the same number of elements, regardless of what the elements are.
mcqs.explanation: Equal sets must contain precisely the same elements; merely having the same cardinality is insufficient. Option B is the misconception because sets {1,2,3} and {a,b,c} have the same size but are not equal. Options A, C, and D correctly describe equality.

mcqs.question: Which pair of sets below are equivalent (i.e., have the same number of elements)?
mcqs.explanation: Equivalent sets are defined by having the same cardinality. Option A has three elements in each set, so they are equivalent. Option B differs (2 vs 3 elements), C are both empty (they are also equivalent but the question asks for a non‑trivial example), and D has 4 vs 3 elements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines the empty set?

options.A: A set that contains no elements.
options.B: A set that contains exactly one element, namely 0.
options.C: A set that contains all natural numbers.
options.D: A set that contains only the empty set as an element.

mcqs.answer: A set that contains no elements.
mcqs.explanation: The empty set, denoted ∅, is the unique set with zero elements. Option B describes a singleton set {0}, not the empty set. Option C is the set of natural numbers, which is infinite. Option D describes a set whose sole element is ∅, which itself is not empty.

mcqs.question: A set that contains a countable number of elements which can be listed completely is called:
mcqs.explanation: A finite set has a limited number of elements; they can be enumerated as a1, a2, …, an for some natural number n. This matches the definition asked. An infinite set cannot be listed completely, a singleton set has exactly one element, and the empty set has none.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines an infinite set?

options.A: A set that contains no elements.
options.B: A set that contains exactly one element.
options.C: A set that has an unbounded number of elements.
options.D: A set that can be placed in one‑to‑one correspondence with the set of natural numbers.

mcqs.answer: A set that can be placed in one‑to‑one correspondence with the set of natural numbers.
mcqs.explanation: An infinite set is one that is not finite; mathematically, it can be put into a bijection with ℕ, showing it has the same cardinality as the natural numbers. Option C is vague, while D gives the precise definition used in set theory. Options A and B describe the empty and singleton sets respectively.

mcqs.question: A singleton set is:

options.A: A set that contains exactly one element.
options.B: A set that contains no elements.
options.C: A set that contains infinitely many elements.
options.D: A set that contains exactly two elements.

mcqs.answer: A set that contains exactly one element.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a singleton set has precisely one member, e.g., {5}. Option B is the empty set, C is an infinite set, and D describes a set of cardinality two.

mcqs.question: Two sets A and B are said to be equal if:

options.A: They contain exactly the same elements.
options.B: They have the same number of elements.
options.C: One is a subset of the other.
options.D: They share at least one common element.

mcqs.answer: They contain exactly the same elements.
mcqs.explanation: Equality of sets requires mutual inclusion: every element of A is in B and every element of B is in A. Hence the sets must have identical members. Having the same cardinality (option B) is insufficient for equality. Options C and D describe subset and intersection concepts, not equality.

mcqs.question: If set A has 5 elements and set B also has 5 elements, which statement is always true?

options.A: A and B are equal sets.
options.B: A and B are equivalent sets.
options.C: A is a subset of B.

mcqs.answer: A and B are equivalent sets.
mcqs.explanation: Equivalent sets are defined solely by having the same cardinality. Since both have 5 elements, they are equivalent regardless of the actual elements. They need not be equal (option A), nor is one necessarily a subset of the other (option C), and they may share elements, so they are not necessarily disjoint (option D).
